Initial magnetic-field probes and regenerative finite-code memory

Scope. The completed nonlinear mean-flux compiler is not automatically a
compiler for arbitrary initial-field data. The following prepares that
different operation using its actually earned register/filter/amplifier
interfaces. It does not read an unknown field or manufacture an additional
magnetic actuator. Simultaneous acquisition and the full long-memory
physical concatenation remain part of a full question.

1. Small-time acquisition can precede erasure

Let the full MHD initial pair have joint H1 norm<=M, M>=1, with unknown
magnetic mean H and arbitrary admissible velocity. For a nonzero integer
wavevector k and coordinate i define
 r_cos(B)=M^-1 int B_i cos(2pi k.x),
 r_sin(B)=M^-1 int B_i sin(2pi k.x).
Both have absolute value<=1. The H1 promise gives |r|<=1/|k|.

During a genuine initial UNFORCED interval of duration t, weak induction
tested against the specified smooth Fourier mode gives, uniformly over
every energy realization,
 |r(B(t))-r(B0)|
 <=C t(|k|^2+M|k|+eta),
as long as t<=1,eta<=1, after enlarging an absolute rational constant.
Indeed scalar diffusion is at most1, total L2 energy gives a bound2M,
and the induction product is bounded in L1 by2||u||2||B||2. No value of
the initial velocity, diffusivity or disturbance is observed. This is
a weak-Fourier-functional bound, not H1 continuity of heat in operator
norm. It controls the actual INITIAL feature, not a redefined later input.

Choose t first from the desired feature error, retained input band and
the paid local H1 threshold. The zero-disturbance reference from the same
unknown H1 initial pair has fixed-order spatial smoothing bounds at t.
The actual rough-disturbance discrepancy is estimated by the existing
two-norm local comparison; eta can be chosen after the physical encoder
parameters. This produces a legitimate smooth proof reference without
assuming the disturbed solution itself has arbitrary Sobolev regularity.
The usual (0,H) eraser cannot precede this operation: it destroys the
nonconstant data to be used later.
